# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (Mar 18, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
The day saw no direct code contributions but significant activity in addressing CI flakiness and a critical bad block issue on Base Mainnet. Discussions on `op-node`'s initial EL Sync UX also continued, with proposals for improved finalization gadgets.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

No direct code changes were merged today.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- **Dependency Updates and Backend mTLS Support:** A new pull request was opened to update the `google.golang.org/grpc` dependency in `/op-ufm` ([#571](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/571)). Additionally, a PR was opened to add backend mTLS support for websocket upstreams in `proxyd` ([#570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/570)).

## CLOSED ISSUES

- **Makefile to Justfile Migration:** The issue tracking the migration of all Makefiles to Justfiles was closed today, indicating the completion of this chore ([#19546](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19546)). All 7 migration PRs have been merged, and CI, scripts, Dockerfiles, and READMEs are updated.
- **Flaky Test Resolution:** The `TestCLIBootstrapForge` flaky test was investigated and closed ([#19627](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19627)). The root cause was identified as a 60-second context timeout in `ExpectSuccessWithNetwork` during contract deployment over a forked Sepolia RPC, which could be exceeded under CI load. A fix increasing helper timeouts to 5 minutes was already in progress and covers this issue.

## NEW ISSUES

- **Kona MessageGraph Configuration:** A new issue was opened regarding Kona's `MessageGraph` using a hardcoded `MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` (7 days) instead of the configurable dependency set value ([#19636](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19636)). This could lead to inconsistent message expiry behavior.
- **Base Mainnet Bad Block:** A critical issue was reported on Base Mainnet concerning a "BAD BLOCK, invalid gas used" error, with detailed system information and `op-node` logs provided ([#778](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/778)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

- **op-node: Initial EL Sync UX and Correctness ([#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/17631))**: Discussion continued on the `op-node`'s behavior of marking the target of initial EL Sync as finalized, even if the block is not actually finalized.
    - `trianglesphere` proposed using the L1 finalized head timestamp minus 12 hours (sequence window) to ensure the finalized head is never set ahead of derivation, though this doesn't guarantee consistency.
    - `karlfloersch` expressed support for the operational simplicity of delaying safe/finalized by the sequencing window to address 80% of the issue.
    - `trianglesphere` further elaborated on a proposal to continue EL sync to the unsafe head and use a different finalization gadget for the finalized head. Options for this gadget include a command-line flag, an RPC URL for a trusted checkpoint provider, looking at L1 for the last finalized head, or an arbitrary delay of 12 hours to 10 days. They lean towards a command-line flag or a 12-hour fallback.
    - `trianglesphere` also clarified that the issue might be triggered while sequencing with EL, but sequencer nodes are usually fully synced. Light CL makes this bug more likely.
- **Non-terminating CI job: memory-all-opn-op-geth ([#19563](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19563))**: The CI job `memory-all-opn-op-geth` continues to experience non-terminating runs.
    - `ajsutton` reported another occurrence where `TestChallengerPlaysGame` timed out after 2 hours. An investigation was launched, noting 3 flakes for this test in `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs`.
    - `ajsutton` opened a draft fix, identifying the root cause as `waitForClaim` and `WaitForCountered` polling loops using a 20-minute timeout context, while internal RPC calls use the base test context with a 2-hour deadline. This leads to indefinite blocking when RPC calls hang due to CI resource contention. The fix involves creating a context-bound copy of the `FaultDisputeGame` binding for polling loops.
    - `ajsutton` also added a data point, noting that the `interop/proofs` package timed out in another job, with `TestChallengerRespondsToMultipleInvalidClaimsEOA` and `TestChallengerPlaysGame` passing before the timeout. Logs showed `l2-proposer` stuck retrying and `supernode` error loops, indicating that acceptance tests creating full L1+L2+supernode systems per test without shared setup contribute to cumulative runtime exceeding the job timeout.
    - `geoknee` suggested that several ongoing PRs might fix this issue and proposed re-evaluating in a few days.
- **Flaky test: `TestSupernodeSameTimestampInvalidTransitive` ([#19570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19570))**: This test continues to be flaky.
    - `maurelian` provided a detailed root cause analysis, identifying a race condition in multi-chain transitive invalidation. The failure mode is a consistent timeout at ~2m46s because the `RewindEngine` gets stuck in a retry loop. This happens when a synthetic payload is rejected with "links to previously rejected block" due to prior invalidation poisoning geth's block rejection cache. The retry is futile as geth won't change its mind.
    - `maurelian` outlined potential fix directions: treating `ErrRewindSyntheticPayloadRejected` as critical, clearing geth's block rejection cache before rewind, using a different rewind strategy, or coordinating multi-chain rewinds.
    - `maurelian` also added CI run context, noting the test timed out after 2m46s.
    - `ajsutton` reopened the issue after observing 4 flakes in recent CI runs and launched an investigation.
